prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1051; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured's vehicle was struck while turning left at an intersection. The claimant reports a back strain and says the impact was sudden and forceful.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 3: Police report and the statements of the scene witnesses place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact. The witnesses did not see the collision itself, so there are no independent eyewitnesses to the sequence of events.

Entry 4: Photographs taken at the scene show the damage to the vehicle, and the pattern of damage lines up with the impact described by the claimant. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection notes.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant by phone. The account of how the collision happened was the same as the one given at first notice, with no changes in the sequence or the details.

Entry 6: The claimant's injury report fits the type and force of the crash. Medical records show the claimant was treated for a complaint in the same area of the back within the last two years, and that prior condition is adding to the current symptoms.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a typical course, with early visits for pain and stiffness and then a gradual reduction in appointments as the claimant improved. The provider's notes describe steady recovery.

Entry 8: Second call with the claimant confirmed the same account of the collision, again without any variation. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been handling communications directly.

Entry 9: File reviewed and summarized for the supervisor. Vehicle damage, injury type, and treatment pattern are consistent with the reported loss, with the prior back condition noted as a factor in the current complaints.
